sentences.zh: 張允登，漢州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yundeng was a man of Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yundeng was from Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三十八年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the thirty-eighth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 歷知咸寧、咸陽，有善政。

translations.literal: He successively served as magistrate of Xianning and Xianyang, and had good administration.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as magistrate of Xianning and Xianyang, where he won praise for effective governance.

sentences.zh: 其成進士，出湯賓尹之門，賓尹弗善也，而東林以賓尹故，惡之。

translations.literal: When he became a jinshi he came from Tang Binyin's school; Binyin did not regard him favorably, and because of Binyin the Donglin faction hated him.
translations.idiomatic: When he took his jinshi degree he had been a student of Tang Binyin, whom he had displeased; the Donglin faction in turn despised him on Binyin's account.

sentences.zh: 舉卓異，得刑部主事，累遷河西兵備副使。

translations.literal: Recommended as outstanding, he obtained the post of principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, and was promoted in succession to military vice commissioner of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Marked out for exceptional merit, he was appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments and was eventually promoted to military vice commissioner of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 鄜、延歲饑，亟遭盜，允登拊循備至，士民德之。

translations.literal: In Fu and Yan'an there were famine year after year and constant bandit raids; Yundeng comforted and provisioned the people with utmost care, and officials and commoners were grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: Famine struck Fu and Yan'an year after year, and bandit raids were constant; Yundeng comforted and supplied the people with every care, and officials and commoners alike were grateful to him.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年閏十一月督餉至甘泉，降卒潛與流賊通，殺知縣郭永固，劫餉。

translations.literal: In the intercalary eleventh month of the fourth year of Chongzhen, while supervising grain transport at Ganquan, surrendered soldiers secretly communicated with roving bandits, killed Magistrate Guo Yonggu, and plundered the supplies.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eleventh month of the fourth year of Chongzhen, while supervising grain transport at Ganquan, surrendered troops secretly colluded with roving bandits, killed Magistrate Guo Yonggu, and seized the supplies.

sentences.zh: 允登力禦，不敵死。

translations.literal: Yundeng resisted with all his strength but could not hold them and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yundeng fought them with all his strength but could not prevail and was killed.

sentences.zh: 鄜人素服迎其喪，哭聲震十里，罷市三日。

translations.literal: The people of Fu came out in plain dress to meet his coffin; lamentation shook the countryside for ten li, and markets were closed for three days.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Fu came out in mourning dress to receive his coffin; wailing was heard for ten li around, and markets were closed for three days.

sentences.zh: 當是時，流賊日熾，總督洪承疇往來奔擊，日不暇給。

translations.literal: At that time the roving bandits grew daily fiercer, and Governor-General Hong Chengchou rushed back and forth in pursuit, with scarcely a moment to spare.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the roving bandits grew fiercer by the day, and Governor-General Hong Chengchou rushed about in pursuit, scarcely able to catch his breath.

sentences.zh: 逾月陷宜君，又陷葭州，僉事郭景嵩死之。

translations.literal: Within a month they took Yijun, then Jiazhou as well; Assistant Commissioner Guo Jingsong died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month they took Yijun and then Jiazhou as well; Assistant Commissioner Guo Jingsong died in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 明年二月陷鄜州，兵備副使郭應響死之。

translations.literal: The following year in the second month they took Fuzhou; Military Vice Commissioner Guo Yingxiang died there.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the second month, they took Fuzhou; Military Vice Commissioner Guo Yingxiang died in the defense.

sentences.zh: 應響，福清人，萬歷丙午舉鄉試第一。

translations.literal: Yingxiang was a native of Fuqing; in the bingwu year of Wanli he ranked first in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Yingxiang was a native of Fuqing; in the bingwu year of Wanli he had ranked first in the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 寧塞余賊來犯，應響禦之，斬賊常山虎等十五人。

translations.literal: When remnants of bandits from Ningsai came to attack, Yingxiang repelled them and beheaded fifteen men including the bandit Changshan Hu.
translations.idiomatic: When bandit remnants from Ningsai came to attack, Yingxiang repelled them and beheaded fifteen men, including the bandit known as Changshan Hu.

sentences.zh: 至是，混天猴率眾夜突至，應響登北關，集士卒拒守，手殺三賊，力不支遂死。

translations.literal: On this occasion Hun Tianhou led his men in a night assault; Yingxiang mounted the North Gate, gathered the soldiers to hold the line, personally killed three bandits, but his strength failed and he died.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion Hun Tianhou led his men in a night assault; Yingxiang mounted the North Gate, rallied the troops to hold the line, and personally killed three bandits before his strength gave out and he fell.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈光祿寺少卿，謚忠烈，予祭葬，蔭一子入監讀書。

translations.literal: When the affair was reported, he was posthumously appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, given the posthumous title Zhonglie, granted funeral rites and sacrifice, and one son was granted enrollment in the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was reported, he was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, given the posthumous title Zhonglie (Loyal and Fierce), granted funeral rites and sacrifice, and one son was granted enrollment in the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 張光奎，澤州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Guangkui was a man of Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guangkui was from Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 仕至山東右參政。

translations.literal: He rose in office to Right Assistant Commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He had risen to the post of Right Assistant Commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 崇禎五年，流賊躪山西，監司王肇生以便宜署歙人吳開先為將，使擊賊，戰澤州城西。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chongzhen, roving bandits overran Shanxi; Supervisor Wang Zhaosheng, acting on emergency authority, appointed Wu Kaixian of She county as general and sent him to attack the bandits; they fought west of Zezhou city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chongzhen, roving bandits overran Shanxi; Supervisor Wang Zhaosheng, exercising emergency powers, appointed Wu Kaixian of She county as general and sent him against the bandits; they fought west of Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 賊敗去，從沁水轉掠陽城。

translations.literal: The bandits were defeated and withdrew; they crossed through Qinshui and turned to plunder Yangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits were beaten and withdrew, then passed through Qinshui and turned to plunder Yangcheng.

sentences.zh: 開先恃勇渡沁，戰北留墩下，擊斬數百人，炮盡無援，一軍盡沒。

translations.literal: Kaixian, trusting in his courage, crossed the Qin River and fought below Beiliu Mound; he struck down several hundred men, but when his cannon fire was exhausted and no reinforcements came, his entire force was wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: Kaixian, trusting in his courage, crossed the Qin and fought below Beiliu Mound, killing several hundred men; but when his ammunition was spent and no reinforcements came, his whole force was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 賊乃再犯澤州，光奎方里居，與兄守備光璽、千總劉自安等率眾固守八日，援兵不至，城陷，並死之。

translations.literal: The bandits then attacked Zezhou again; Guangkui was then living at home, and together with his elder brother the garrison commander Guangxi, chiliarch Liu Zi'an, and others led the populace in a steadfast defense for eight days; reinforcements did not arrive, the city fell, and they all died.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits then attacked Zezhou again; Guangkui was living at home at the time and, together with his elder brother the garrison commander Guangxi, chiliarch Liu Zi'an, and others, led the people in a stubborn defense for eight days; when no relief came and the city fell, they all perished.

sentences.zh: 澤，大州也，遠近為震動。

translations.literal: Ze was a great prefecture, and the shock spread far and near.
translations.idiomatic: Ze was a major prefecture, and the shock was felt far and wide.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈光祿卿，光璽等贈恤有差。

translations.literal: When reported, Guangkui was posthumously made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Guangxi and the others received posthumous favors of varying degree.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was reported, Guangkui was posthumously made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Guangxi and the others received posthumous honors of varying degree.

sentences.zh: 是歲，紫金梁等寇遼州，裏居行人楊於楷與主事張友程，佐知州信陽李呈章拒守，力屈城陷，於楷被執，罵賊死。

translations.literal: That year Zijin Liang and others raided Liaozhou; Yang Yukai, a metropolitan graduate living at home, and Principal Secretary Zhang Youcheng assisted Prefect Li Chengzhang of Xinyang in defense; their strength gave out and the city fell; Yukai was captured and died cursing the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zijin Liang and others raided Liaozhou; Yang Yukai, a metropolitan graduate living in retirement, and Principal Secretary Zhang Youcheng assisted Prefect Li Chengzhang of Xinyang in the defense; when their strength failed and the city fell, Yukai was taken and died cursing the bandits.

sentences.zh: 呈章、友程及舉人趙一亨、侯標並死之。

translations.literal: Chengzhang, Youcheng, and juren Zhao Yiheng and Hou Biao all died as well.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhang, Youcheng, and the juren Zhao Yiheng and Hou Biao all died as well.

sentences.zh: 明年六月，賊陷和順，裏居昌平副使樂濟眾被傷，不屈，投井死。

translations.literal: The following year in the sixth month the bandits took Heshun; Yue Jizhong, a vice commissioner of Changping living at home, was wounded, refused to yield, and threw himself into a well to die.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the sixth month, the bandits took Heshun; Yue Jizhong, a vice commissioner of Changping living in retirement, was wounded, refused to submit, and threw himself into a well to die.

sentences.zh: 贈於楷光祿少卿，濟眾太仆少卿。

translations.literal: Yukai was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Jizhong was made Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Yukai was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Jizhong was made Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 有徐明揚者，浮梁人，由選貢生為平順知縣。

translations.literal: There was Xu Mingyang, a native of Fuliang, who through selection as a tribute student became magistrate of Pingshun.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Xu Mingyang, a native of Fuliang, who through selection as a tribute student had become magistrate of Pingshun.

sentences.zh: 六年四月，賊來犯，設策守禦，城破不屈死。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the sixth year the bandits came to attack; he devised measures for defense, and when the city fell he refused to submit and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the sixth year the bandits attacked; he devised measures of defense, and when the city fell he refused to yield and died.

sentences.zh: 李中正，盧氏人。

translations.literal: Li Zhongzheng was a man of Lushi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongzheng was from Lushi.

sentences.zh: 萬歷末，舉會試，以天啟二年赴廷對，授承天府推官，遷兵部主事。

translations.literal: At the end of Wanli he passed the metropolitan examination; in the second year of Tianqi he attended the palace examination and was appointed investigating censor of Chengtian Prefecture, then transferred to principal secretary in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Wanli reign he passed the metropolitan examination; in the second year of Tianqi he attended the palace examination and was appointed investigating censor of Chengtian Prefecture, then transferred to principal secretary in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，謝病歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign he resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 六年，群盜大亂河北。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, bands of robbers threw Hebei into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, bands of robbers threw Hebei into great disorder.

sentences.zh: 其冬，乘冰渡河，遂由澠池犯盧氏。

translations.literal: That winter they crossed the river on the ice and advanced through Mianchi to attack Lushi.
translations.idiomatic: That winter they crossed the river on the ice and advanced through Mianchi to attack Lushi.

sentences.zh: 中州承平久，不設備。

translations.literal: The central provinces had long been at peace and made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: The central provinces had long been at peace and were unprepared.

sentences.zh: 驟聞賊至，吏民惶駴，知縣金會嘉棄城遁。

translations.literal: Suddenly hearing the bandits had arrived, officials and people were terrified; Magistrate Jin Huijia abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When word suddenly came that the bandits had arrived, officials and people were terrified; Magistrate Jin Huijia abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 十二月，賊入城，中正勒家眾及里中壯士奮擊，眾寡不敵，力戰死。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the bandits entered the city; Zhongzheng rallied his household and the stalwarts of the neighborhood to fight fiercely; outnumbered, he battled to the death.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the bandits entered the city; Zhongzheng rallied his household and the stalwarts of the neighborhood to fight fiercely; outnumbered, he battled to the death.

sentences.zh: 賊縱掠城中，執舉人靳謙書，使跪，不屈，大罵而死。

translations.literal: The bandits plundered the city at will; they seized the juren Jin Qianshu, forced him to kneel, but he would not submit and died after a great curse.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits plundered the city at will; they seized the juren Jin Qianshu and forced him to kneel, but he would not submit and died after cursing them fiercely.

sentences.zh: 賊以是冬始入河南，自是屢陷名城，殺將吏無算，鄉官舉貢多被難。

translations.literal: The bandits entered Henan for the first time that winter; thereafter they repeatedly took famous cities, killed countless commanders and officials, and many local gentry and tribute students suffered in the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits entered Henan for the first time that winter; thereafter they repeatedly took famous cities, killed commanders and officials beyond count, and many local gentry and tribute students perished in the calamity.

sentences.zh: 其宜陽馬足輕，靈寶許煇，新安劉君培、馬山、李登英，偃師裴君合，陜州張我正、張我德，孟津孫挺生，嵩縣傅世濟、李佩玉，上蔡劉時寵輩，則先後以布衣抗節顯。

translations.literal: Among them Ma Zuqing of Yiyang, Xu Hui of Lingbao, Liu Junpei, Ma Shan, and Li Dengying of Xin'an, Pei Junhe of Yanshi, Zhang Wozheng and Zhang Wode of Shaanzhou, Sun Tingsheng of Mengjin, Fu Shiji and Li Peiyu of Song county, Liu Shichong of Shangcai and others in turn won fame as commoners who upheld their integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Among them Ma Zuqing of Yiyang, Xu Hui of Lingbao, Liu Junpei, Ma Shan, and Li Dengying of Xin'an, Pei Junhe of Yanshi, Zhang Wozheng and Zhang Wode of Shaanzhou, Sun Tingsheng of Mengjin, Fu Shiji and Li Peiyu of Song county, Liu Shichong of Shangcai and others in turn won fame as commoners who upheld their integrity.

sentences.zh: 足輕，性孝友。

translations.literal: Zuqing was by nature filial and brotherly.
translations.idiomatic: Zuqing was by nature filial and devoted to his brothers.

sentences.zh: 弟惑婦言，迫分產，乃取田磽薄者自予。

translations.literal: His younger brother was misled by his wife's words and pressed for a division of property; Zuqing therefore took for himself the barren and poor fields.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother, swayed by his wife, pressed for a division of the estate; Zuqing therefore kept for himself the barren and poor fields.

sentences.zh: 萬歷末，歲大兇，出粟六百石以振，焚券千余。

translations.literal: At the end of Wanli, when the year was greatly famine-stricken, he gave out six hundred shi of grain for relief and burned more than a thousand debt notes.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Wanli reign, in a year of severe famine, he distributed six hundred shi of grain for relief and burned more than a thousand debt notes.

sentences.zh: 崇禎六年冬，流賊渡河而南，挈家避之石龍崖。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year of Chongzhen, roving bandits crossed the river southward; he took his family to seek refuge at Shilong Cliff.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the sixth year of Chongzhen, as roving bandits crossed the river southward, he took his family to seek refuge at Shilong Cliff.

sentences.zh: 三女皆殊色，慮賊汙，悉投崖死。

translations.literal: His three daughters were all of exceptional beauty; fearing defilement by the bandits, they all threw themselves from the cliff to die.
translations.idiomatic: His three daughters were all exceptionally beautiful; fearing defilement by the bandits, they all threw themselves from the cliff to their deaths.

sentences.zh: 足輕被執，厲聲大罵。

translations.literal: Zuqing was seized and cursed them loudly.
translations.idiomatic: Zuqing was seized and cursed them in a thunderous voice.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，並三子殺之。

translations.literal: The bandits were enraged and killed him together with his three sons.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits were enraged and killed him together with his three sons.

sentences.zh: 家眾皆遇害，惟存次子駿一人，後登鄉薦。

translations.literal: All the household perished; only the second son Jun survived, and later passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: The entire household perished; only the second son Jun survived, and later passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 煇為縣陰陽官，為賊所掠，大罵見殺。

translations.literal: Hui served as the county yin-yang official; he was seized by bandits, cursed them fiercely, and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Hui served as the county yin-yang official; seized by bandits, he cursed them fiercely and was killed.

sentences.zh: 君培有義行，攜子及從孫避難，道遇賊，欲殺其從孫。

translations.literal: Junpei was known for righteous conduct; fleeing with his son and nephew, he met bandits on the road who wished to kill his nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Junpei was known for righteous conduct; while fleeing with his son and nephew, he met bandits on the road who wished to kill his nephew.

sentences.zh: 君培曰：「我尚有男，此子乃遺孤，幸舍之而殺我。」

translations.literal: Junpei said: I still have a son; this boy is an orphan left in my care—please spare him and kill me instead.
translations.idiomatic: Junpei said, "I still have a son; this boy is an orphan left in my care—please spare him and kill me instead.

sentences.zh: 賊如其言，二子獲免。

translations.literal: The bandits did as he said, and the two boys were spared.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits did as he asked, and the two boys were spared.

sentences.zh: 山性剛直，土寇於大中陷新安，獲山，使負米。

translations.literal: Shan was by nature stern and upright; when local bandits under Yu Dazhong took Xin'an, they seized Shan and made him carry rice.
translations.idiomatic: Shan was by nature stern and upright; when local bandits under Yu Dazhong took Xin'an, they seized him and made him carry rice.

sentences.zh: 叱曰：「我天朝百性，肯為賊負米邪！」

translations.literal: He shouted: I am a subject of the Heavenly Dynasty—would I carry rice for bandits!
translations.idiomatic: He shouted, "I am a subject of the Heavenly Dynasty—would I carry rice for bandits!

sentences.zh: 大罵而死。

translations.literal: He cursed them fiercely and died.
translations.idiomatic: He cursed them fiercely and was killed.

sentences.zh: 登英亦以罵賊死。

translations.literal: Dengying likewise died cursing the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Dengying likewise died after cursing the bandits.

sentences.zh: 君合幼孤，母苦節，孝養惟謹。

translations.literal: Junhe was orphaned young; his mother lived in bitter widowhood, and he supported her with the utmost filial care.
translations.idiomatic: Junhe was orphaned young; his mother lived in bitter widowhood, and he supported her with the utmost filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 賊至，聚眾保沙岸寨。

translations.literal: When bandits came, he gathered the people to defend Sha'an Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits came, he gathered the people to defend Sha'an Stockade.

sentences.zh: 攻圍十晝夜不克，說之降，大罵不從。

translations.literal: They besieged it for ten days and nights without success, urged him to surrender, but he cursed them and refused.
translations.idiomatic: They besieged it for ten days and nights without success, urged him to surrender, but he cursed them and refused.

sentences.zh: 寨破，被磔。

translations.literal: When the stockade fell, he was dismembered.
translations.idiomatic: When the stockade fell, he was dismembered.

sentences.zh: 我正素豪俠，集眾保鄉里，一方賴之。

translations.literal: Wozheng had always been bold and chivalrous; he gathered the people to protect the countryside, and the whole region relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Wozheng had always been bold and chivalrous; he gathered the people to protect the countryside, and the whole region relied on him.

sentences.zh: 十四年勒眾禦賊，馘三人。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he led the people to resist bandits and took three heads.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he led the people against the bandits and killed three of them.

sentences.zh: 俄賊大至，眾悉奔，奮臂獨戰。

translations.literal: Soon a great force of bandits arrived; the crowd all fled, but he fought alone with bared arms.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a great force of bandits arrived; everyone fled, but he fought on alone.

sentences.zh: 賊愛其男，欲生致之，詬罵自刎死。

translations.literal: The bandits admired his courage and wished to take him alive; he reviled them and killed himself by cutting his throat.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits admired his courage and wished to take him alive; he reviled them and cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 我德知賊至，恐妻子受辱，驅一家二十七人登樓自焚。

translations.literal: Wode, learning the bandits had come, feared his wife and children would be dishonored and drove twenty-seven members of his household up a tower to burn themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Wode, learning the bandits had come, feared his wife and children would be dishonored and drove twenty-seven members of his household up a tower to burn themselves alive.

sentences.zh: 挺生精星術，預卜十五年有寇禍，編茅河渚以居。

translations.literal: Tingsheng was skilled in astrology; he foretold that in fifteen years there would be bandit calamity and built a thatched hut on the riverbank to live in.
translations.idiomatic: Tingsheng was skilled in astrology; he foretold bandit calamity within fifteen years and built a thatched hut on the riverbank to live in.

sentences.zh: 賊蹤跡得之，語其妻梁氏曰：「此匹夫徇義之秋也。」

translations.literal: The bandits tracked him down; he said to his wife Lady Liang: This is the season for a common man to die for righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits tracked him down; he said to his wife Lady Liang, "This is the season for a common man to die for righteousness.

sentences.zh: 夫婦對泣，詬賊而死。

translations.literal: Husband and wife wept facing each other, reviled the bandits, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Husband and wife wept together, reviled the bandits, and died.

sentences.zh: 世濟與兄世舟並為土寇於大中所執，將殺之。

translations.literal: Shiji and his elder brother Shizhou were both seized by local bandits under Yu Dazhong and were about to be killed.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji and his elder brother Shizhou were both seized by local bandits under Yu Dazhong and were about to be killed.

sentences.zh: 兄弟相抱泣，賊議釋其一，世濟即奪賊刀自殺，世舟獲免。

translations.literal: The brothers embraced and wept; the bandits debated releasing one of them; Shiji immediately seized a bandit's knife and killed himself, and Shizhou was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers embraced and wept; the bandits debated releasing one of them; Shiji immediately seized a bandit's knife and killed himself, and Shizhou was spared.

sentences.zh: 佩玉者，御史興元孫也。

translations.literal: Peiyu was the grandson of Censor Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Peiyu was the grandson of Censor Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 崇禎末，中州盡殘，佩玉結遺民捍鄉井，與鄰寨相掎角，往往尾賊後，奪其輜重。

translations.literal: At the end of Chongzhen the central provinces were utterly devastated; Peiyu rallied survivors to defend their villages, coordinated with neighboring stockades, and often followed behind the bandits to seize their baggage trains.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Chongzhen reign the central provinces were utterly devastated; Peiyu rallied survivors to defend their villages, coordinated with neighboring stockades, and often followed the bandits to seize their baggage trains.

sentences.zh: 賊憚之，不敢出其境。

translations.literal: The bandits feared him and dared not leave his territory.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits feared him and dared not leave his territory.

sentences.zh: 後大舉圍別寨，佩玉往救，力戰而死，裏人聚哭之。

translations.literal: Later, when bandits besieged another stockade on a large scale, Peiyu went to the rescue, fought fiercely, and died; the villagers gathered to mourn him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when bandits besieged another stockade in force, Peiyu went to the rescue, fought fiercely, and fell; the villagers gathered to mourn him.

sentences.zh: 時寵有孝行。

translations.literal: Shichong was known for filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong was known for filial conduct.

sentences.zh: 賊陷城，其父宗祀以年老不能行，命之速避，遂自殺。

translations.literal: When bandits took the city, his father Zongsi, too old to flee, ordered him to escape quickly and then killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits took the city, his father Zongsi, too old to flee, urged him to escape quickly and then killed himself.

sentences.zh: 時寵慟哭，刺殺一子、三女，夫婦並自剄。

translations.literal: Shichong wept in anguish, stabbed one son and three daughters to death, and he and his wife both cut their throats.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong wept in anguish, stabbed one son and three daughters to death, and he and his wife both cut their throats.

sentences.zh: 其妹適歸寧，亦從死，一家死者八人。

translations.literal: His sister, visiting home on a return trip, died with them as well; eight people in the family perished.
translations.idiomatic: His sister, visiting home on a return trip, died with them as well; eight people in the family perished.

sentences.zh: 方國儒，字道醇，歙縣人。

translations.literal: Fang Guoru, styled Daochun, was a native of She county.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Guoru, styled Daochun, was from She county.

sentences.zh: 四歲失父，奉母以孝聞。

translations.literal: He lost his father at four and was known for supporting his mother with filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father at the age of four and was known for supporting his mother with filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年舉於鄉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianqi he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 崇禎間，授保康知縣。

translations.literal: During Chongzhen he was appointed magistrate of Baokang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign he was appointed magistrate of Baokang.

sentences.zh: 流賊大入湖廣，將吏率望風先奔。

translations.literal: Roving bandits poured into Huguang in force, and commanders and officials for the most part fled at the first rumor.
translations.idiomatic: Roving bandits poured into Huguang in force, and commanders and officials for the most part fled at the first rumor.

sentences.zh: 保康小邑素無兵，七年正月賊至，國儒急率鄉兵出禦，力不支，城遂陷。

translations.literal: Baokang was a small county that had never had troops; in the first month of the seventh year the bandits arrived, and Guoru urgently led local militia out to resist, but his strength failed and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Baokang was a small county that had never had troops; in the first month of the seventh year the bandits arrived, and Guoru urgently led local militia out to resist, but could not hold them and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 亡何，賊退，國儒還入城。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits withdrew, and Guoru returned to the city.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the bandits withdrew, and Guoru returned to the city.

sentences.zh: 逾月復至，督吏民固拒。

translations.literal: After more than a month they came again, and he urged officials and people to hold firm in resistance.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month they came again, and he urged officials and people to hold firm in resistance.

sentences.zh: 賊至益眾，復陷。

translations.literal: The bandits came in even greater numbers, and the city fell again.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits came in even greater numbers, and the city fell again.

sentences.zh: 國儒官服坐堂上，被執大罵，身中七刃死。

translations.literal: Guoru sat in official dress in the hall; seized, he cursed them fiercely and died after seven blade wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Guoru sat in official dress in the hall; seized, he cursed them fiercely and died after seven blade wounds.

sentences.zh: 賊陷竹谿，訓導王紹正死之。

translations.literal: When bandits took Zhuxi, Instructor Wang Shaozheng died in the defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits took Zhuxi, Instructor Wang Shaozheng died in the defense.

sentences.zh: 谷城舉人常存畏會試赴京，道遇賊，欲劫為首領，罵不絕口死。

translations.literal: Chang Cunwei of Gucheng, a juren on his way to the capital for the metropolitan examination, met bandits on the road; they wished to seize him as their leader, but he cursed them without cease until he died.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Cunwei of Gucheng, a juren on his way to the capital for the metropolitan examination, met bandits on the road; they wished to seize him as their leader, but he cursed them without cease until he died.

sentences.zh: 他賊犯興山，知縣劉定國堅守。

translations.literal: Other bandits attacked Xingshan; Magistrate Liu Dingguo held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Other bandits attacked Xingshan; Magistrate Liu Dingguo held firm.

sentences.zh: 城將陷，遣吏懷印送上官，罵賊死。

translations.literal: As the city was about to fall, he sent an official bearing the seal to his superior, cursed the bandits, and died.
translations.idiomatic: As the city was about to fall, he sent an official bearing the seal to his superior, cursed the bandits, and died.

sentences.zh: 何承光，貴州鎮遠人。

translations.literal: He Chengguang was a native of Zhenyuan in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengguang was from Zhenyuan in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十年舉於鄉。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year of Wanli he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year of Wanli he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，歷夔州同知。

translations.literal: During Chongzhen he served in succession as subprefect of Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign he served as subprefect of Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 七年二月，賊由荊州入夔門，犯夔州。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year, bandits entered through Kuimen from Jingzhou and attacked Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventh year, bandits entered through Kuimen from Jingzhou and attacked Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 副使周士登在涪州，城中倉猝無備，通判、推官、知縣悉遁。

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner Zhou Shideng was at Fuzhou; within the city there was no preparation in the emergency, and the subprefect, investigating censor, and magistrate all fled.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commissioner Zhou Shideng was at Fuzhou; the city was wholly unprepared, and the subprefect, investigating censor, and magistrate all fled.

sentences.zh: 承光攝府事，率吏民固守，力竭城陷。

translations.literal: Chengguang took charge of prefectural affairs, led officials and people in a steadfast defense, and when his strength was exhausted the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Chengguang took charge of prefectural affairs, led officials and people in a steadfast defense, and when his strength was exhausted the city fell.

sentences.zh: 承光整冠帶危坐，賊入殺之，投屍於江。

translations.literal: Chengguang straightened his cap and sash and sat upright; the bandits entered and killed him and threw his body into the river.
translations.idiomatic: Chengguang straightened his cap and sash and sat upright; the bandits entered, killed him, and threw his body into the river.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈承光夔州知府。

translations.literal: When the affair was reported, Chengguang was posthumously made prefect of Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was reported, Chengguang was posthumously made prefect of Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 自賊起陜西，轉寇山西、畿輔、河南、北及湖廣、四川，陷州縣以數十許，未有破大郡者，至是天下為震動。

translations.literal: From the time the bandits rose in Shaanxi, they turned to raid Shanxi, the capital region, Henan, and northward into Huguang and Sichuan, taking dozens of prefectures and counties; never before had they broken a great prefecture—now the whole realm was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: From the time the bandits rose in Shaanxi, they turned to raid Shanxi, the capital region, Henan, and northward into Huguang and Sichuan, taking dozens of prefectures and counties; never before had they broken a great prefecture—now the whole realm was shaken.

sentences.zh: 其他部自漢中犯大寧，知縣高日臨見勢弱不能守，嚙指書牒乞援上官，率眾禦之北門。

translations.literal: Another band entered from Hanzhong to attack Daning; Magistrate Gao Rilin, seeing his force was too weak to hold, bit his finger and wrote a dispatch begging aid from his superior, then led the people to defend the North Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Another band entered from Hanzhong to attack Daning; Magistrate Gao Rilin, seeing his force was too weak to hold, bit his finger and wrote a dispatch begging aid from his superior, then led the people to defend the North Gate.

sentences.zh: 兵敗被執，大罵不屈，賊碎其體焚之。

translations.literal: His troops were defeated and he was seized; he cursed them fiercely and would not yield; the bandits dismembered his body and burned it.
translations.idiomatic: His troops were defeated and he was seized; he cursed them fiercely and would not yield; the bandits dismembered his body and burned it.

sentences.zh: 訓導高錫及妻女，巡檢陳國俊及妻，皆遇害。

translations.literal: Instructor Gao Xi and his wife and daughters, and Inspector Chen Guojun and his wife, all perished.
translations.idiomatic: Instructor Gao Xi and his wife and daughters, and Inspector Chen Guojun and his wife, all perished.

sentences.zh: 日臨，字儼若，鄱陽恩貢生。

translations.literal: Rilin, styled Yanruo, was an enfeoffed tribute student of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: Rilin, styled Yanruo, was an enfeoffed tribute student of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 賊陷夔州，他賊即以次日陷巫山，通江巡檢郭纘化陣沒，通江指揮王永年力戰死。

translations.literal: When bandits took Kuizhou, other bandits took Wushan the very next day; Tongjiang Inspector Guo Zuanhua fell in battle, and Tongjiang Commander Wang Yongnian fought fiercely and died.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits took Kuizhou, other bandits took Wushan the very next day; Tongjiang Inspector Guo Zuanhua fell in battle, and Tongjiang Commander Wang Yongnian fought fiercely and died.

sentences.zh: 至四月，守備郭震辰、指揮田實擊賊百丈關，兵敗被執，罵賊死。

translations.literal: By the fourth month, Garrison Commander Guo Zhenchen and Commander Tian Shi attacked bandits at Baizhang Pass; their troops were defeated and they were seized; they cursed the bandits and died.
translations.idiomatic: By the fourth month, Garrison Commander Guo Zhenchen and Commander Tian Shi attacked bandits at Baizhang Pass; their troops were defeated and they were seized; they cursed the bandits and died.

sentences.zh: 龐瑜，字堅白，公安人。

translations.literal: Pang Yu, styled Jianbai, was a native of Gong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Yu, styled Jianbai, was from Gong'an.

sentences.zh: 家貧，躬耕自給。

translations.literal: His family was poor; he farmed with his own hands to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor; he farmed with his own hands to support himself.

sentences.zh: 夏轉水灌田，執書從牛後，朗誦不輟。

translations.literal: In summer, turning the water to irrigate the fields, he held a book behind the ox and recited aloud without cease.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, while turning the water to irrigate the fields, he held a book behind the ox and recited aloud without cease.

sentences.zh: 由歲貢生授京山訓導。

translations.literal: Through the annual tribute student route he was appointed instructor of Jingshan.
translations.idiomatic: Through the annual tribute student route he was appointed instructor of Jingshan.

sentences.zh: 崇禎七年擢陜西崇信知縣。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Chongzhen he was promoted to magistrate of Chongxin in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Chongzhen he was promoted to magistrate of Chongxin in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 縣無城，兵荒，貧民止百余戶。

translations.literal: The county had no wall; amid war and famine, poor households numbered only a little over a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The county had no wall; amid war and famine, poor households numbered only a little over a hundred.

sentences.zh: 瑜知賊必至，言於監司陸夢龍，以無兵辭。

translations.literal: Yu knew bandits would certainly come and spoke to Supervisor Lu Menglong, declining on grounds of having no troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yu knew bandits would certainly come and spoke to Supervisor Lu Menglong, declining on grounds of having no troops.

sentences.zh: 瑜集士民築土垣以守，流涕誓死職。

translations.literal: Yu gathered gentry and people to build earthen walls for defense, weeping as he swore to die at his post.
translations.idiomatic: Yu gathered gentry and people to build earthen walls for defense, weeping as he swore to die at his post.

sentences.zh: 閏八月天大雨，土垣盡圮。

translations.literal: In the intercalary eighth month heaven sent great rain, and the earthen walls all collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eighth month a great rain fell, and the earthen walls all collapsed.

sentences.zh: 賊掩至，瑜急解印遣家人賫送上官，端坐堂上以待。

translations.literal: Bandits came upon them suddenly; Yu urgently removed the seal and sent his family to deliver it to his superior, then sat upright in the hall to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits came upon them suddenly; Yu urgently removed the seal and sent his family to deliver it to his superior, then sat upright in the hall to await them.

sentences.zh: 賊至，捽令跪。

translations.literal: When the bandits arrived, they seized him and ordered him to kneel.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits arrived, they seized him and ordered him to kneel.

sentences.zh: 瑜罵曰：「賊奴敢辱官長！」

translations.literal: Yu cursed: Bandit slaves dare insult an official!
translations.idiomatic: Yu cursed, "Bandit slaves dare insult an official!

sentences.zh: 拔刀脅之，罵益厲。

translations.literal: They drew knives to threaten him, but his curses grew fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: They drew knives to threaten him, but his curses grew fiercer.

sentences.zh: 賊掠城中無所有，執至野外，剖心裂屍而去。

translations.literal: The bandits found nothing worth plundering in the city; they took him to the wilds, cut open his heart, dismembered his corpse, and left.
translations.idiomatic: Finding nothing worth plundering in the city, the bandits took him to the wilds, cut open his heart, dismembered his corpse, and left.

sentences.zh: 贈固原知州。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made prefect of Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made prefect of Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 時賊盡趨秦中，長吏多殉城者。

translations.literal: At that time the bandits all pressed into Qinzhong, and many senior officials died with their cities.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the bandits all pressed into Qinzhong, and many senior officials died with their cities.

sentences.zh: 山陽陷，知縣董三謨，黎平舉人也，及父嗣成、弟三元俱死之，妻李氏亦攜子女偕死。

translations.literal: When Shanyang fell, Magistrate Dong Sanmo, a juren of Liping, died together with his father Sicheng and brother Sanyuan; his wife Lady Li also took her children and died with them.
translations.idiomatic: When Shanyang fell, Magistrate Dong Sanmo, a juren of Liping, died together with his father Sicheng and brother Sanyuan; his wife Lady Li also took her children and died with them.

sentences.zh: 贈光祿丞，立祠，與嗣成、三元並祀，妻女建坊旌表。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; a shrine was established, and he was worshipped together with Sicheng and Sanyuan; his wife and daughters were honored with a commemorative arch.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; a shrine was established, and he was worshipped together with Sicheng and Sanyuan; his wife and daughters were honored with a commemorative arch.

sentences.zh: 吉永祚，輝縣人。

translations.literal: Ji Yongzuo was a native of Huixian.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Yongzuo was from Huixian.

sentences.zh: 為鳳縣主簿，謝事將歸。

translations.literal: He served as registrar of Feng county and had resigned his post and was about to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He served as registrar of Feng county and had resigned his post and was about to return home.

sentences.zh: 會賊至，知縣棄城遁，永祚倡義拒守。

translations.literal: Just then bandits arrived; the magistrate abandoned the city and fled, and Yongzuo took the lead in organizing resistance.
translations.idiomatic: Just then bandits arrived; the magistrate abandoned the city and fled, and Yongzuo took the lead in organizing resistance.

sentences.zh: 城陷，北面再拜曰：「臣雖小吏，嘗食祿於朝，不敢以謝事逃責。」

translations.literal: When the city fell, he bowed twice facing north and said: Though I am a minor official, I have received salary from the court and dare not use my resignation to escape responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, he bowed twice facing north and said, "Though I am a minor official, I have received salary from the court and dare not use my resignation to escape responsibility.

sentences.zh: 大罵死之。

translations.literal: He cursed them fiercely and died.
translations.idiomatic: He cursed them fiercely and died.

sentences.zh: 子士樞、士模皆死。

translations.literal: His sons Shishu and Shimo both died.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Shishu and Shimo both died.

sentences.zh: 教諭李之蔚、鄉官魏炳亦不屈死。

translations.literal: Instructor Li Zhiwei and local official Wei Bing likewise refused to yield and died.
translations.idiomatic: Instructor Li Zhiwei and local official Wei Bing likewise refused to yield and died.

sentences.zh: 永祚贈漢中衛經歷，余贈恤有差。

translations.literal: Yongzuo was posthumously made secretary of Hanzhong Guard; the others received posthumous favors of varying degree.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzuo was posthumously made secretary of Hanzhong Guard; the others received posthumous honors of varying degree.

sentences.zh: 婁琇知涇州。

translations.literal: Lou Xiu was prefect of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Xiu was prefect of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 閏八月，城陷死，贈太仆少卿。

translations.literal: In the intercalary eighth month the city fell and he died; he was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eighth month the city fell and he died; he was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 蒲來舉知甘泉。

translations.literal: Pu Laiju was magistrate of Ganquan.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Laiju was magistrate of Ganquan.

sentences.zh: 賊來犯，守備孫守法等擁兵不救。

translations.literal: When bandits came to attack, Garrison Commander Sun Shoufa and others held troops but did not come to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits came to attack, Garrison Commander Sun Shoufa and others held troops but did not come to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 城破，來舉手刃一賊，傷六賊而後死。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Laiju killed one bandit with his own hand, wounded six bandits, and then died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Laiju killed one bandit with his own hand, wounded six bandits, and then fell.

sentences.zh: 贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 呂鳴世，福建人。

translations.literal: Lü Mingshi was a native of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Mingshi was from Fujian.

sentences.zh: 由恩貢生為麟遊知縣。

translations.literal: Through the rank of tribute student by grace he became magistrate of Linyou.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a tribute student by grace and was appointed magistrate of Linyou.

sentences.zh: 兵燹後，拊居民有恩。

translations.literal: After the warfare and conflagration, he soothed the residents with kindness.
translations.idiomatic: After the devastation of war, he showed kindness in comforting the townspeople.

sentences.zh: 城陷，賊不忍加害，自絕食六日卒。

translations.literal: When the city fell, the bandits could not bear to harm him; he abstained from food for six days and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, the bandits could not bring themselves to harm him; he starved himself for six days and died.

sentences.zh: 有宋緒湯者，耀州諸生，被獲，大罵死。

translations.literal: There was one Song Xutang, a student of Yaozhou; captured, he cursed fiercely and died.
translations.idiomatic: One Song Xutang, a licentiate of Yaozhou, was captured; he cursed the bandits fiercely and was killed.

sentences.zh: 尹夢鰲，雲南太和人。

translations.literal: Yin Meng'ao was a native of Taihe in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Meng'ao was from Taihe in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 萬歷時舉於鄉。

translations.literal: During the Wanli reign he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign he passed the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中知潁州。

translations.literal: During Chongzhen he was prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign he served as prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 八年正月方謁上官於鳳陽，聞流賊大至，立馳還。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year, while paying calls on superiors at Fengyang, he heard that roving bandits were approaching in force and immediately galloped back.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year, while visiting his superiors at Fengyang, he heard that roving bandits were approaching in great numbers and immediately rode back at full speed.

sentences.zh: 賊已抵城下，乃偕通判趙士寬率民固守。

translations.literal: The bandits had already reached the foot of the city wall; he then together with Assistant Prefect Zhao Shikuan led the people in staunch defense.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits had already reached the city walls; he joined Assistant Prefect Zhao Shikuan in leading the people in a staunch defense.

sentences.zh: 城北有高樓間城中，諸生劉廷傳請先據之，夢鰲以為然。

translations.literal: North of the city there was a tall tower overlooking the city; licentiate Liu Tingchuan asked to occupy it first, and Meng'ao agreed.
translations.idiomatic: North of the city stood a tall tower overlooking the inner city; licentiate Liu Tingchuan proposed seizing it first, and Meng'ao agreed.

sentences.zh: 而廷傳所統皆市人，不可用。

translations.literal: But those under Tingchuan's command were all townspeople and could not be used.
translations.idiomatic: But the men under Tingchuan's command were all townspeople and proved unusable.

sentences.zh: 賊遂據樓以攻，且鑿城，頹數丈，城上人皆走，止之不可。

translations.literal: The bandits then seized the tower to attack, and also dug at the wall, collapsing several zhang; those atop the wall all fled, and could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits then seized the tower and used it to attack, while also burrowing into the wall until several zhang collapsed; the defenders on the wall all fled and could not be restrained.

sentences.zh: 夢鰲持大刀，獨當城壞處，殺賊十余人，身被數刃。

translations.literal: Meng'ao wielded a great sword, alone blocking the breached section, killed more than ten bandits, and was cut several times.
translations.idiomatic: Meng'ao took up a broadsword and alone stood at the breach, killing more than ten bandits before sustaining several wounds.

sentences.zh: 賊眾畢登，遂投城下烏龍潭死，弟侄七人皆死之。

translations.literal: When the bandits had all climbed up, he then threw himself into Wulong Pond below the city and died; seven nephews and younger brothers all died with him.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits had all scaled the walls, he threw himself into Wulong Pond below the city and drowned; seven nephews and younger brothers died with him.

sentences.zh: 廷傳者，故布政使九光從子，任俠好義，亦罵賊死。

translations.literal: Tingchuan was the nephew of the former provincial administration commissioner Jiuguang; chivalrous and fond of righteousness, he likewise cursed the bandits and died.
translations.idiomatic: Tingchuan was the nephew of the former provincial administration commissioner Jiuguang; a man of chivalrous spirit who loved righteousness, he likewise cursed the bandits and was killed.

sentences.zh: 九光子廷石分守西城，中賊刃未絕，口授友人方略，令繕牘上當事，旋卒。

translations.literal: Jiuguang's son Tingshi held the western sector of the city separately; struck by a bandit's blade but not yet dead, he orally dictated strategy to a friend, had a document drafted and sent to the authorities, and soon expired.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuguang's son Tingshi defended the western wall; though struck by a bandit's blade and not yet dead, he orally dictated a plan of defense to a friend, had it written up and sent to the authorities, and soon expired.

sentences.zh: 士寬，字汝良，掖縣人。

translations.literal: Shikuan, styled Ruliang, was a native of Ye county.
translations.idiomatic: Shikuan, styled Ruliang, was from Ye county.

sentences.zh: 由門蔭為鳳陽通判，駐潁州。

translations.literal: Through hereditary privilege he became assistant prefect of Fengyang, stationed at Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he was appointed assistant prefect of Fengyang and stationed at Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 以正旦詣郡城，聞警，一日夜馳三百里返州。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day he went to the district seat; hearing the alarm, he galloped three hundred li in one day and night to return to the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day he had gone to the district seat; on hearing the alarm, he rode three hundred li in a single day and night to return to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 城陷，率家眾巷戰，力竭，亦投烏龍潭死。

translations.literal: When the city fell, he led his household in street fighting until strength was exhausted, and likewise threw himself into Wulong Pond and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, he led his household in street fighting until exhausted, then likewise threw himself into Wulong Pond and died.

sentences.zh: 妻李攜三女登樓自焚，仆王丹亦罵賊死。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Li took three daughters up a tower and burned themselves; servant Wang Dan likewise cursed the bandits and died.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Li took three daughters upstairs and burned themselves to death; his servant Wang Dan likewise cursed the bandits and was killed.

sentences.zh: 鄉官尚書張鶴鳴、弟副使鶴勝、子大同，中書舍人田之穎，知縣劉道遠，光祿署正李生白，訓導丁嘉遇，舉人郭三傑，諸生韓光祿等，皆死之。

translations.literal: Local official and former Minister Zhang Heming, his younger brother Vice Commissioner Hesheng, his son Datong, Secretariat Drafter Tian Zhiying, Magistrate Liu Daoyuan, Director of Imperial Banquets Li Shengbai, Instructor Ding Jiayu, juren Guo Sanjie, licentiate Han Guanglu and others—all died.
translations.idiomatic: The local official and former Minister Zhang Heming, his younger brother Vice Commissioner Hesheng, his son Datong, Secretariat Drafter Tian Zhiying, Magistrate Liu Daoyuan, Director of Imperial Banquets Li Shengbai, Instructor Ding Jiayu, juren Guo Sanjie, licentiate Han Guanglu, and others all perished.

sentences.zh: 光祖，進士獻策父也，被執，賊捽使跪。

translations.literal: Guangzu was the father of jinshi Xiances; captured, the bandits dragged him and made him kneel.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzu was the father of jinshi Xiances; when captured, the bandits dragged him forward and forced him to kneel.

sentences.zh: 叱曰：「吾生平讀書，止知忠義。」

translations.literal: He shouted: In all my life of reading books, I know only loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He shouted, "All my life I have read books and know only loyalty and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 遂大罵。

translations.literal: He then cursed them fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: He then cursed them fiercely.

sentences.zh: 賊殺之，碎其屍。

translations.literal: The bandits killed him and smashed his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits killed him and dismembered his body.

sentences.zh: 妻武偕一妹、一女並獻策妻李赴井死。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Wu, together with one younger sister and one daughter, along with Xiances's wife Lady Li, went to a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Wu, together with a younger sister and a daughter, along with Xiances's wife Lady Li, threw themselves into a well and died.

sentences.zh: 妾李方有娠，賊剖腹剔胎死。

translations.literal: Concubine Li was just pregnant; the bandits cut open her belly and removed the fetus and she died.
translations.idiomatic: Concubine Li was pregnant; the bandits cut open her belly, extracted the fetus, and killed her.

sentences.zh: 次子定策、孫日曦罵賊死，獨獻策獲存。

translations.literal: Second son Dingce and grandson Rixi cursed the bandits and died; only Xiances survived.
translations.idiomatic: Second son Dingce and grandson Rixi cursed the bandits and were killed; only Xiances survived.

sentences.zh: 時被難者共一百三人，城中婦人死節者三十七人，烈女八人。

translations.literal: At that time those who suffered calamity numbered altogether one hundred and three persons; women in the city who died in fidelity to chastity numbered thirty-seven, and heroic women eight.
translations.idiomatic: In all, one hundred and three people perished in the catastrophe; thirty-seven women in the city died defending their chastity, and eight were counted as heroic martyrs.

sentences.zh: 潁州忠烈，稱獨盛雲。

translations.literal: Yingzhou's loyal martyrs—in renown it alone flourished.
translations.idiomatic: In its display of loyal martyrdom, Yingzhou stood alone in renown.

sentences.zh: 潁州衛隸河南，流賊至，指揮李從師、王廷俊，千戶孫升、田三震，百戶羅元慶、田得民、王之麟俱乘城戰死。

translations.literal: Yingzhou Guard was subordinate to Henan; when roving bandits arrived, Commanders Li Congshi and Wang Tingjun, Battalion Commanders Sun Sheng and Tian Sanzhen, Platoon Commanders Luo Yuanqing, Tian Demin, and Wang Zhilin all mounted the walls and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou Guard fell under Henan jurisdiction; when roving bandits arrived, Commanders Li Congshi and Wang Tingjun, Battalion Commanders Sun Sheng and Tian Sanzhen, and Platoon Commanders Luo Yuanqing, Tian Demin, and Wang Zhilin all took to the walls and died fighting.

sentences.zh: 賊既陷潁州，屠其民。

translations.literal: Once the bandits had taken Yingzhou, they slaughtered its people.
translations.idiomatic: After the bandits captured Yingzhou, they massacred its people.

sentences.zh: 其別部即以是月由壽州犯鳳陽。

translations.literal: Their separate division that same month proceeded from Shouzhou to attack Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: That same month a separate bandit column advanced from Shouzhou against Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 鳳陽故無城，中都留守朱國相率指揮袁瑞徵、呂承蔭、郭希聖、張鵬翼、周時望、李郁、嶽光祚，千戶陳弘祖、陳其忠、金龍化等，以兵三千逆賊上窯山，多斬獲。

translations.literal: Fengyang originally had no city wall; Metropolitan Garrison Commandant Zhu Guoxiang led Commanders Yuan Ruizheng, Lü Chengyin, Guo Xisheng, Zhang Pengyi, Zhou Shiwang, Li Yu, and Yue Guangzuo, Battalion Commanders Chen Hongzu, Chen Qizhong, Jin Longhua and others, with three thousand troops to intercept the bandits at Shangyao Mountain, and killed and captured many.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyang had never had city walls; Metropolitan Garrison Commandant Zhu Guoxiang led Commanders Yuan Ruizheng, Lü Chengyin, Guo Xisheng, Zhang Pengyi, Zhou Shiwang, Li Yu, and Yue Guangzuo, along with Battalion Commanders Chen Hongzu, Chen Qizhong, Jin Longhua, and others, with three thousand troops to intercept the bandits on Shangyao Mountain, inflicting many kills and captures.

sentences.zh: 俄賊數萬至，矢集如猬，遂敗，國相自刎死，余皆陣沒。

translations.literal: Soon tens of thousands of bandits arrived; arrows gathered thick as a hedgehog, and they were defeated; Guoxiang cut his own throat and died, and the rest all perished on the battlefield.
translations.idiomatic: Soon tens of thousands of bandits arrived; arrows fell thick as bristles on a hedgehog, and the defenders were routed; Guoxiang slit his own throat and died, and the rest all fell on the field.

sentences.zh: 賊遂犯皇陵，大肆焚掠。

translations.literal: The bandits then assaulted the imperial mausoleum and burned and plundered on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits then raided the imperial mausoleum, burning and looting on a vast scale.

sentences.zh: 知府顏容暄囚服匿於獄，釋囚獲之，容暄大罵，賊杖殺之。

translations.literal: Prefect Yan Rongxuan, in prison garb, hid in the jail; released prisoners seized him; Rongxuan cursed fiercely, and the bandits beat him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Yan Rongxuan, dressed in convict's garb, hid in the jail; released prisoners found him; Rongxuan cursed them fiercely, and the bandits beat him to death with staves.

sentences.zh: 血浸石階，宛如其像，滌之不滅。

translations.literal: Blood soaked the stone steps, exactly like his portrait; washed, it would not vanish.
translations.idiomatic: Blood soaked the stone steps in a likeness of his portrait; washing could not remove it.

sentences.zh: 士民乃取石立冢，建祠奉祀。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners then took stone to erect a tomb and built a shrine to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: The officials and commoners then carved stone to raise a tomb and built a shrine where he was worshipped.

sentences.zh: 推官萬文英臥病，賊索之。

translations.literal: Administrative Aide Wan Wenying lay ill; the bandits sought him.
translations.idiomatic: Administrative Aide Wan Wenying lay ill in bed; the bandits came searching for him.

sentences.zh: 子元亨，年十六，泣語父曰：「兒不得復事親矣！」

translations.literal: His son Yuanheng, age sixteen, weeping said to his father: I can no longer serve my parent!
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanheng, aged sixteen, wept and said to his father, "I shall never again be able to serve you as a son!

sentences.zh: 出門呼曰：「若索官，何為？

translations.literal: Going out the door he called: If you seek an official, for what purpose?
translations.idiomatic: Stepping outside, he called out, "If you are looking for an official, why bother?

sentences.zh: 我即官也。

translations.literal: I am the official.
translations.idiomatic: I am the official.

sentences.zh: 賊縶之。

translations.literal: The bandits seized him.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits seized him.

sentences.zh: 顧見其師萬師尹亦被縶，紿賊曰：「若欲得者，官爾。

translations.literal: Looking back he saw his teacher Wan Shiyin also seized; he deceived the bandits saying: If you wish to get him, the official is he.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that his teacher Wan Shiyin had also been seized, he deceived the bandits, saying, "If you want the official, it is he.

sentences.zh: 何縶此賤隸？」

translations.literal: Why seize this lowly servant?
translations.idiomatic: Why seize this worthless servant?"

sentences.zh: 賊遂釋之。

translations.literal: The bandits then released him.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits then released Shiyin.

sentences.zh: 元亨乃極口大罵。

translations.literal: Yuanheng then cursed them with all his mouth's force.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanheng then cursed them without restraint.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，斷脛死，文英獲免。

translations.literal: The bandits in anger severed his shins and he died; Wenying was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the bandits severed his legs and killed him; Wenying was spared.

sentences.zh: 容暄，漳浦人。

translations.literal: Rongxuan was a native of Zhangpu.
translations.idiomatic: Rongxuan was from Zhangpu.

sentences.zh: 文英，南昌人。

translations.literal: Wenying was a native of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Wenying was from Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 皆進士。

translations.literal: Both were jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Both were jinshi degree holders.

sentences.zh: 一時同死者，千戶陳永齡、百戶盛可學等四十一人，諸生六十六人。

translations.literal: Those who died together at that time numbered forty-one, including Battalion Commander Chen Yongling and Platoon Commander Sheng Kexue and others, and sixty-six licentiates.
translations.idiomatic: Those who died at the same time included forty-one men such as Battalion Commander Chen Yongling and Platoon Commander Sheng Kexue, and sixty-six licentiates.

sentences.zh: 舉人蔣思宸聞變，投繯死。

translations.literal: Juren Jiang Sichen, on hearing the calamity, hanged himself and died.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing of the disaster, juren Jiang Sichen hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 後給事中林正亨錄上其狀，贈夢鰲光祿少卿，士寬光祿丞，余贈恤有差。

translations.literal: Later Supervising Secretary Lin Zhengheng recorded and submitted their accounts; Meng'ao was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Shikuan Director of the same court, and the others received posthumous favors of varying degree.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Supervising Secretary Lin Zhengheng memorialized the court with a full account; Meng'ao was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Shikuan Director of the same court, and the others received posthumous honors of varying degree.

sentences.zh: 盧謙，字吉甫，廬江人。

translations.literal: Lu Qian, styled Jifu, was a native of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qian, styled Jifu, was from Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三十二年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the thirty-second year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the thirty-second year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 授永豐知縣。

translations.literal: Appointed magistrate of Yongfeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Yongfeng.

sentences.zh: 擢御史，出為江西右參政，引疾歸。

translations.literal: Promoted to censor, then sent out as Right Vice Commissioner of Jiangxi; he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to censor and then appointed Right Vice Commissioner of Jiangxi; citing illness, he retired to his home.

sentences.zh: 崇禎八年二月，流賊犯廬江，士民具財帛求免，賊偽許之。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year of Chongzhen, roving bandits attacked Lujiang; officials and commoners prepared money and silks seeking exemption; the bandits falsely promised it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eighth year of Chongzhen, roving bandits attacked Lujiang; the officials and people gathered money and goods to buy their safety, and the bandits falsely agreed.

sentences.zh: 俄襲陷其城，謙服命服，危坐中門。

translations.literal: Soon they raided and took the city; Qian wore the robe of office and sat upright at the central gate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they stormed and captured the city; Qian put on his official robes and sat upright at the main gate.

sentences.zh: 賊至，欲屈之，罵曰：「吾朝廷憲臣，肯為賊屈邪？

translations.literal: When bandits arrived and wished to humiliate him, he cursed: I am a disciplinary official of the court—would I bow to bandits?
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits came seeking to break him, he cursed them, "I am a disciplinary official of the court—would I bow to bandits?

sentences.zh: 鼠輩滅亡在即，安敢無禮！」

translations.literal: You rats will perish any moment—how dare you be rude!
translations.idiomatic: You vermin are doomed to perish—how dare you treat me with disrespect!

sentences.zh: 賊怒殺之，投屍於池，池水盡赤。

translations.literal: The bandits in anger killed him, threw his corpse into a pool, and the pool water turned entirely red.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the bandits killed him and threw his body into a pool, turning the water completely red.

sentences.zh: 舉人張受、畢尹周亦不屈被殺。

translations.literal: Juren Zhang Shou and Bi Yinzhou likewise refused to yield and were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Juren Zhang Shou and Bi Yinzhou likewise refused to submit and were killed.

sentences.zh: 是年正月，賊陷霍丘，縣丞張有俊，教諭倪可大，訓導何炳，鄉官田既庭、戴廷對，舉人王毓貞死焉。

translations.literal: In the first month of that year, bandits took Huoqiu; Assistant Magistrate Zhang Youjun, Instructor Ni Keda, Sub-Instructor He Bing, local officials Tian Jiting and Dai Tingdui, and juren Wang Yuzhen died there.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of that year, bandits captured Huoqiu; Assistant Magistrate Zhang Youjun, Instructor Ni Keda, Sub-Instructor He Bing, local officials Tian Jiting and Dai Tingdui, and juren Wang Yuzhen all perished.

sentences.zh: 賊陷巢縣，知縣嚴覺被執不屈，一門皆死。

translations.literal: Bandits took Chaoxian; Magistrate Yan Jue was captured and would not yield; his whole household died.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits captured Chaoxian, Magistrate Yan Jue was seized but refused to yield; his entire household perished.

sentences.zh: 二月犯太湖，知縣金應元據城東大濠以守。

translations.literal: In the second month they attacked Taihu; Magistrate Jin Yingyuan held the great moat east of the city to defend.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month they attacked Taihu; Magistrate Jin Yingyuan defended from the great moat east of the city.

sentences.zh: 奸人導賊渡濠，執應元，斫之未殊，自經死。

translations.literal: A traitor guided the bandits across the moat; they seized Yingyuan, hacked him but did not kill him outright; he hanged himself and died.
translations.idiomatic: A collaborator guided the bandits across the moat; they seized Yingyuan and hacked at him without finishing the job; he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 訓導扈永寧亦死之。

translations.literal: Sub-Instructor Hu Yongning likewise died.
translations.idiomatic: Sub-Instructor Hu Yongning died as well.

sentences.zh: 謙贈光祿卿，余贈恤如制。

translations.literal: Qian was posthumously made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; the others received posthumous favors according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was posthumously made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; the others received posthumous honors according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 覺，歸安人。

translations.literal: Jue was a native of Gui'an.
translations.idiomatic: Jue was from Gui'an.

sentences.zh: 應元，浙江山陰人。

translations.literal: Yingyuan was a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yingyuan was from Shanyin in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 皆舉人。

translations.literal: Both were juren.
translations.idiomatic: Both were juren degree holders.

sentences.zh: 龔元祥，字子禎，長洲人。

translations.literal: Gong Yuanxiang, styled Zizhen, was a native of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Yuanxiang, styled Zizhen, was from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 舉於鄉。

translations.literal: Passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年為霍山教諭，厲廉隅，以名教自任，與訓導姚允恭友善。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongzhen he was instructor of Huoshan; he sternly kept to integrity, took upon himself the teaching of moral doctrine, and was on friendly terms with Sub-Instructor Yao Yungong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chongzhen he served as instructor of Huoshan; he strictly upheld personal integrity, held himself accountable to the teachings of moral order, and was close friends with Sub-Instructor Yao Yungong.

sentences.zh: 八年，賊陷鳳陽，元祥偕縣令守禦。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when bandits took Fengyang, Yuanxiang together with the county magistrate defended.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when bandits captured Fengyang, Yuanxiang joined the county magistrate in mounting a defense.

sentences.zh: 賊掩至，令逸去，元祥督士民固守。

translations.literal: Bandits came by surprise; the magistrate fled; Yuanxiang supervised officials and commoners in staunch defense.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits struck without warning; the magistrate fled, and Yuanxiang rallied the officials and people in a staunch defense.

sentences.zh: 或勸之避，元祥曰：「食祿而避難，不忠。

translations.literal: Some urged him to flee; Yuanxiang said: Receiving salary yet fleeing calamity is disloyalty.
translations.idiomatic: When some urged him to flee, Yuanxiang said, "To draw a salary yet flee from danger is disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 臨危而棄城，不義。

translations.literal: Facing peril yet abandoning the city is unrighteous.
translations.idiomatic: To abandon the city in a crisis is unrighteous.

sentences.zh: 吾平日講說者謂何？

translations.literal: What then of what I ordinarily lecture and expound?
translations.idiomatic: What then were all my daily lectures about?

sentences.zh: 倘不測，死爾。」

translations.literal: If the unexpected occurs, death—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: If the worst comes, then death it shall be.

sentences.zh: 及賊陷城，元祥整衣冠危坐。

translations.literal: When the bandits took the city, Yuanxiang straightened his cap and garments and sat upright.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits captured the city, Yuanxiang straightened his cap and robes and sat in dignified composure.

sentences.zh: 賊至，侃侃諭以大義。

translations.literal: When bandits arrived, he calmly expounded great principle to them.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits arrived, he calmly reasoned with them on the obligations of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 賊欲屈之，厲聲曰：「死即死，賊輩何敢辱我！」

translations.literal: When bandits wished to humiliate him, he said in a stern voice: Die then die—how dare you bandits insult me!
translations.idiomatic: When they sought to break him, he said in a fierce voice, "If I must die, then die I shall—how dare you bandits dishonor me!

sentences.zh: 賊怒，執之去，罵不絕口，遂遇害。

translations.literal: The bandits in anger seized him and took him away; he cursed without cease and was thus killed.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the bandits seized him and dragged him away; he never stopped cursing and was killed.

sentences.zh: 子炳衡號呼罵賊，賊又殺之。

translations.literal: His son Bingheng shouted and cursed the bandits; the bandits killed him too.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bingheng cried out and cursed the bandits; they killed him as well.

sentences.zh: 閱五日，允恭斂其屍，即自縊，適令至，解免。

translations.literal: After five days, Yungong gathered his corpse, then hanged himself; just then an order arrived and he was released and spared.
translations.idiomatic: Five days later, Yungong collected their bodies, then hanged himself; an order arrived just then and he was cut down and spared.

sentences.zh: 越日，賊復入，允恭卒死之。

translations.literal: The next day bandits entered again; Yungong at last died.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the bandits entered again, and Yungong finally perished.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈元祥國子助教，建祠曰忠孝，以其子配。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Yuanxiang was posthumously made Assistant Instructor of the Directorate of Education; a shrine called Loyalty and Filial Piety was built, with his son enshrined alongside him.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, Yuanxiang was posthumously made Assistant Instructor of the Directorate of Education; a shrine called Loyalty and Filial Piety was erected, with his son enshrined beside him.

sentences.zh: 允恭亦被旌。

translations.literal: Yungong likewise received commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Yungong was also officially commended.

sentences.zh: 王信，陜西寧州人。

translations.literal: Wang Xin was a native of Ningzhou in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xin was from Ningzhou in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 父歿，廬墓三年。

translations.literal: When his father died, he kept vigil at the tomb for three years.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he lived by the tomb in mourning for three years.

sentences.zh: 母歿，信年已六十，足不逾閾者三年。

translations.literal: When his mother died, Xin was already sixty; for three years his feet did not cross the threshold.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, Xin was already sixty; for three years he did not step beyond his threshold.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，由歲貢生除靈璧訓導，遷真陽知縣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen, through senior tribute student rank he was appointed instructor of Lingbi, then transferred to magistrate of Zhenyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongzhen reign, he entered service as a senior tribute student and was appointed instructor of Lingbi, then promoted to magistrate of Zhenyang.

sentences.zh: 八年二月出撫土寇，會流賊猝至，被執，使諭降羅山、真陽。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year he went out to pacify local bandits; roving bandits suddenly arrived; he was captured and made to urge the surrender of Luoshan and Zhenyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eighth year he went out to pacify local bandits; roving bandits suddenly arrived, seized him, and forced him to call for the surrender of Luoshan and Zhenyang.

sentences.zh: 信大罵不從，斷頭剖腹而死。

translations.literal: Xin cursed fiercely and refused; they severed his head and cut open his belly and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Xin cursed them fiercely and refused; they cut off his head, disemboweled him, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 閱四日，其子來覓，猶舒指握子手。

translations.literal: After four days, his son came searching for him; he still extended his fingers and grasped his son's hand.
translations.idiomatic: Four days later, when his son came looking for him, he was still able to stretch out his fingers and clasp his son's hand.

sentences.zh: 贈光祿丞，建祠奉祀。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; a shrine was built for his worship.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and a shrine was erected for his worship.

sentences.zh: 史記言，字司直，當塗人。

translations.literal: Shi Jiyan, courtesy name Sizhi, was a native of Dangtu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jiyan, whose courtesy name was Sizhi, was from Dangtu.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中舉人，由長沙知縣遷知陜州。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate in the Chongzhen reign, he rose from magistrate of Changsha to prefect of Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the provincial examination in the Chongzhen reign, he rose from magistrate of Changsha to prefect of Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 陜當賊沖，記言出私財募士，聘少室僧訓練之。

translations.literal: Shaanzhou lay on the bandit route; Jiyan spent private funds to recruit men and hired Shaoshi monks to train them.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanzhou lay on the main bandit route; Jiyan spent his own money to recruit troops and hired monks from Shaoshi to drill them.

sentences.zh: 八年冬十一月，流賊犯陜，記言禦之，斬數十級，生擒二十余人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter in the eighth year, roving bandits attacked Shaanzhou; Jiyan repelled them, beheaded dozens, and captured more than twenty alive.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the eighth year, roving bandits attacked Shaanzhou; Jiyan drove them off, beheaded dozens, and took more than twenty alive.

sentences.zh: 老回回憤，率數萬人攻城，不克，乘雪夜來襲，而所練士方調他郡，城遂陷。

translations.literal: Lao Huihui, enraged, led tens of thousands to attack the city without success; taking advantage of a snowy night he made a surprise attack, while the trained troops had just been transferred to another prefecture, and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Lao Huihui led tens of thousands to attack the city but failed; then on a snowy night he launched a surprise raid while Jiyan's trained troops had been dispatched to another prefecture, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 記言縱火自焚，兩僧掖之出曰：「死此，何以自明？」

translations.literal: Jiyan set fire to burn himself; two monks pulled him out and said: If I die here, how can I prove my innocence?
translations.idiomatic: Jiyan set himself on fire; two monks pulled him out and said, "If you die here, how will you clear your name?

sentences.zh: 乃越女墻下。

translations.literal: Then he went over the parapet wall.
translations.idiomatic: Then he climbed over the outer wall.

sentences.zh: 賊追獲之，令降，叱曰：「有死知州，無降知州也！」

translations.literal: Bandits pursued and captured him, ordering him to surrender; he shouted: There are dead prefects, but no prefects who surrender!
translations.idiomatic: The bandits pursued and captured him and ordered him to surrender; he shouted, "There are dead prefects, but no prefects who surrender!

sentences.zh: 遂被殺。

translations.literal: He was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: He was then killed.

sentences.zh: 指揮李君賜殺數賊而死。

translations.literal: Commander Li Junci killed several bandits and died.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Li Junci killed several bandits before he himself was killed.

sentences.zh: 訓導王誠心，裏居教諭張敏行、姚良弼，指揮楊道泰、阮我疆，鎮撫陳三元，亦不屈死。

translations.literal: Instructor Wang Chengxin, home-residing instructor Zhang Minxing and Yao Liangbi, commanders Yang Daotai and Ruan Wojiang, and garrison officer Chen Sanyuan likewise refused to submit and died.
translations.idiomatic: Instructor Wang Chengxin, home-residing instructors Zhang Minxing and Yao Liangbi, commanders Yang Daotai and Ruan Wojiang, and garrison officer Chen Sanyuan likewise refused to yield and died.

sentences.zh: 是月，賊陷盧氏，知縣白楹自剄。

translations.literal: That month bandits took Lushi; Magistrate Bai Ying cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: That same month the bandits took Lushi; Magistrate Bai Ying slit his own throat.

sentences.zh: 十年九月陷澠池，知縣李邁林死之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the tenth year Mianchi fell; Magistrate Li Mailin died there.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the tenth year Mianchi fell, and Magistrate Li Mailin died defending it.

sentences.zh: 記言贈光祿少卿，余贈恤有差。

translations.literal: Jiyan was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; the others received posthumous honors of varying degree.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyan was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; the others received posthumous honors of varying degree.

sentences.zh: 梁誌仁，南京人，保定侯銘之裔也。

translations.literal: Liang Zhiren was a Nanjing native and a descendant of Marquis Ming of Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Zhiren was from Nanjing and a descendant of Marquis Ming of Baoding.

sentences.zh: 萬歷末年舉於鄉。

translations.literal: In the late Wanli reign he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Wanli reign he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 崇禎六年授衡陽知縣，調羅田。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Chongzhen he was appointed magistrate of Hengyang, then transferred to Luotian.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Chongzhen he was appointed magistrate of Hengyang and later transferred to Luotian.

sentences.zh: 賊大擾湖廣，誌仁日夕儆備。

translations.literal: Bandits greatly ravaged Huguang; Zhiren kept watch day and night.
translations.idiomatic: As bandits ravaged Huguang, Zhiren remained on constant alert day and night.

sentences.zh: 羅汝才謂左右曰：「羅田城小易克，然梁君長者，吾不忍加兵。

translations.literal: Luo Rucai said to those around him: Luotian is a small city easy to take, yet Magistrate Liang is a man of virtue—I cannot bear to send troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Rucai said to his followers, "Luotian is a small city and easy to take, but Magistrate Liang is a man of worth—I cannot bring myself to attack him.

sentences.zh: 俟其去，當取之。」

translations.literal: Wait until he leaves, then we shall take it.
translations.idiomatic: When he is gone, we shall take it.

sentences.zh: 會邑豪江猶龍與賊通，誌仁捕下獄。

translations.literal: It happened that local magnate Jiang Youlong was in contact with the bandits; Zhiren arrested him and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Just then a local magnate, Jiang Youlong, was found colluding with the bandits; Zhiren had him arrested and thrown in prison.

sentences.zh: 猶龍知必死，潛導汝才別校來攻。

translations.literal: Youlong knew he would surely die and secretly guided one of Rucai's subordinate commanders to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he would surely be executed, Youlong secretly guided one of Rucai's subordinate commanders to launch an attack.

sentences.zh: 八年二月猝攻城。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year they suddenly attacked the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eighth year they launched a sudden assault on the city.

sentences.zh: 誌仁急偕典史單思仁、教諭吳鳳來、訓導盧大受督民守禦。
